reader.requirement: When an exponentiation in an arithmetic expression violates §1985:VI.6.2.3 GR5 (a zero base with an exponent not greater than zero, or a negative base whose power has no real result), the arithmetic operation ends and a size error condition exists: with ON SIZE ERROR every affected resultant keeps its prior value and the phrase runs (NOT ON SIZE ERROR ignored); without the phrase the resultants are undefined and control goes to the end of the statement, the program continuing; a negative base with a real result (odd root) is no violation, and of two real results the positive one is returned (GR5b).

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.NegativeBaseRequiresIntegerExponent (from 2002): at 85 a negative base with a non-integer exponent is a size error only when no real result exists (BoundPower realRoots = true); from 2002 any non-integer exponent of a negative base is EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION

DialectBehavior.UnphrasedSizeErrorIsFatal (from 2002): at 85 an unphrased size error is caught, the resultant left unchanged and the program continues; from 2002 it is the fatal EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION

reader.edition-search: grep NegativeBaseRequiresIntegerExponent|UnphrasedSizeErrorIsFatal|SIZE-EXPONENTIATION over the compiler and runtime; the zero-base screen (CobolPower.ScreenRule6) and the phrase handling with ON SIZE ERROR are the same at every edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: (-8) ** 0.2 is the real root -1.5157 with NOT ON SIZE ERROR at 85 and a size error at 2023; COMPUTE X = 0 ** 0 with no phrase continues at 85 and terminates the run unit with EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION (fatal) at 2023.

reader.notes: Two edition arms serve this rule at 85 and both match the 1985 text: BindPower keeps real roots of negative bases (GR5c), and EmitArith catches an unphrased size error and continues instead of raising the fatal 2002+ exception condition. With the phrase, every resultant of the statement stays unchanged and NOT ON SIZE ERROR is skipped, as GR1 and the phrase rules require. Re-read (wave 20262147 group A, kb/Work PB2628): the zero-base screen and the binary64 power moved unchanged from CobolIntrinsics (RealArgs.cs) into the value library as CobolPower.ScreenRule6 and CobolPower.Binary64; every stored probe re-run at the pin prints what it printed at the first read.
